name: Witch's Revelation: Great Youkai's Instruction
description: You encounter Yae Miko at Barbeloth's fortune-telling booth...

dialogs.content: Oh, look... Miko's over there. Paimon gets the feeling things are about to get stressful...
You remember the Mikawa Flower Festival, right? Sure, everything turned out for the best, but it was a real headache to get there...
And she made us sign ourselves away.
But not this time... Hehe, we're not the ones doing labor, so we definitely won't—
Keep your voice down...
#Well, well... {NICKNAME}, Paimon. To think we'd run into each other all the way out here in Fontaine. So, what are you—
...Whoa! M—Miko! Did you hear that just now?
No, I didn't hear a thing. But judging by your expression, I doubt it was anything... flattering?
No, no, it's not like that! We're really happy to see you, Miko. Hehehe... What brings you to Fontaine, anyway?
(Well that was an awkward change of subject...)
Why else would a poor, overworked Editor-in-Chief like me be here? I'm toiling away on Yae Publishing House business, of course.
I had just bought a box of new books and was planning to take them back for my editors to study...
When who should I see but an old friend of mine lingering at this fortune-telling booth for the longest time.
Back home, she rarely visits the shrine to draw fortune slips, so her sudden interest in fortune-telling was quite the surprise...
Still, while strolling around the city, I overheard people talking about an unusually accurate fortune-teller out here in the countryside.
So, I came to get a reading, if only to... satisfy my curiosity.
Huh? You're finished already? Why didn't you say so sooner!?
What card did you draw?
My, my, taking such an interest in my future, are we? Hehe, if you want to know, I might be persuaded to let you see. However, you'll have to pay a price.
Let me think... Ah! How about you sign on with Yae Publishing House? You can compile your adventures into a thrilling novel.
Following the latest naming trends, we could call it, "I Picked Up Emergency Food at the Start, and Now I'm Invincible." Oh, we're going to sell so many copies!
It would need to be a pretty thick book...
Who cares? As long as it's entertaining, you can make it as long as you want. I once published a light novel called "The Horizon Beyond the Paradox."
That book was as thick as a dictionary and spanned eight volumes. Then there were three companion guides and six spin-offs — stack them all up and they'd reach the ceiling.
If you manage to churn out that much, then I, Editor-in-Chief, will edit it all personally. What do you say?
You just want to rush my drafts!
Interesting... So, you don't want to see which card I drew, then?
I've suddenly lost all interest...
Yes! It turns out we're not that—
Oh, well, here it is.
According to Lady Barbeloth... it's "reversed Justice."
I didn't see that, I covered my eyes!
You don't want to see? Very well... Since you have so little interest in divination, the next time you come for a fortune slip, don't expect me to help you draw.
Come to think of it, you two have been visiting the shrine quite often lately to hang prayer plaques, haven't you? How about...
That's a great card to draw!
*sigh* Seriously!?
So it would seem, but alas, the Justice card I drew is reversed... Does that mean I'm some sort of outlaw, Lady Barbeloth?
The card is named Justice, but it doesn't represent a just or unjust person — at least not in a conventional sense.
Perhaps it would be better to say... Since it's currently reversed, it represents a "dishonest" person.
Dishonest? There must be some mistake. I'm always honest when helping these two interpret their fortune slips... Isn't that right?
#All Paimon knows is that whenever Miko helps {NICKNAME} draw fortune slips, it's always "Great Fortune"...
#That's because of {M#his}{F#her} good luck. Or at least, {M#his}{F#her} good luck whenever {M#he}{F#she}'s by my side.
Luck... Now there's a fine choice of words. Reversed Justice does indeed symbolize a distorted sort of cause and effect, imbalance, dishonesty... and dissatisfaction.
As a youkai, you above all should understand. After all, the birth of a youkai is indelibly tied to desire.
A yearning for something, an uncompleted dream, some unfinished undertaking, the pull of a certain emotion...
All it takes is the slightest catalyst for these unsatisfied desires to take root and grow, and sprout unexpected offshoots.
And you, a great youkai of Inazuma, likely have a greater desire than most buried within your heart...
But that's the limit of what I can see. After all, you only drew one card. What's more, reversed Justice is known to be good at concealing lies, whether from others or oneself.

How delightfully mystifying... Sounds just like something a shrine maiden might say when interpreting fortune slips. I certainly wasn't expecting to pick up any new jargon on this trip, but that one is quite good.
Still, as good as it is, it doesn't really align with our shrine's way of doing things. So, perhaps I'd better not teach it to the shrine maidens after all.
Anyway, thank you for the divination, Lady Mage. Should you ever have the chance, do pay a visit to the Grand Narukami Shrine and allow me to return the favor. What do you say?
I'm afraid my hydromancy keeps me far too busy. I simply can't spare the time to dip my toes into other forms of fortune-telling.
Though your fortune slips sound like something Nicole and Alice would enjoy. I'll be sure to tell them all about you.
Wonderful. When the time comes, I shall personally preside over the drawing of fortune slips for your friends.
I assure you, everyone will draw the most auspicious slips.
Justice... It's got a nice ring to it!
I didn't hear that, I covered my ears!
Sorry, but no. I still have adventuring to do...
(Miko really got us this time...)
